Own question: Baroni cites Hillerup 2011 (PMID 21467556, confirmed) as ref 28, once (PDF p5), grouped with a neuroblastoma-cell study as 'some in vitro studies' supporting dose-dependent neurotoxicity (Hillerup is in vivo). It never describes Hillerup or names it when stating its own result, but it sides with Leuschner 'unlike studies that support the hypothesis that articaine has neurotoxic potential' and concludes the neurotoxicity hypothesis 'was not confirmed' and that 'articaine is not toxic to the nervous structure' - a contrary conclusion from a different design (mucosal injection beside the mental nerve, not intraneural; one marketed concentration; qualitative H&E inflammation score at 24 h vs Hillerup's evoked potentials and stereology at 3 weeks). On the recorded elements ('a finding or conclusion contradicting') C050 is refuted; on a reading limited to disputing Hillerup's measurement it would stay narrowed (stated in the reason). Hillerup & Jensen 2006 (ref 13) is cited four times as paraesthesia background.
